name: Agostinho Neto Memorial (Memorial Dr. António Agostinho Neto)
funding: State Budget transfers fund this public establishment under the Presidency, plus space hire, fees, publications and donations. Mansudae redesigned and built it from 2005; it opened in 2012.

name: Museo Casa sobre el Arroyo (Casa del Puente)
funding: The national state bought the house in 2012 and passed it to the city. The Ministry of Public Works paid over ARS 72M for the restoration, reopened April 2023.

name: Boyd House II (Robin Boyd Foundation)
funding: Robin Boyd Foundation revenue AUD 435k in 2023-24: donations 137k, grants 36k, partnerships 30k. Partners include Brickworks, Maddocks and Arup; donor trusts include Mori Provan and Isaacson Davis.

name: Rose Seidler House
funding: Owned by the NSW Government and run by Museums of History NSW (successor to the Historic Houses Trust), a statutory body with a 2024-25 budget of A$73.6M.

name: Domenig Steinhaus
funding: STEINHAUS Günther Domenig Privatstiftung receives subsidies from Land Kärnten (culture) and the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport. Gemeinde Steindorf and HTL Villach give in-kind sponsoring.

name: Das Rote Wien im Waschsalon Karl-Marx-Hof
funding: Run by Verein Sammlung Rotes Wien. Stadt Wien gives an annual subsidy and the insurer Wiener Städtische supports it. Wien Tourismus shows as a partner logo.

name: Haus Wittgenstein (Bulgarian Cultural Institute)
funding: The Bulgarian state bought the house in 1975 and runs it as the Bulgarian Cultural Institute, the embassy's cultural department. Both countries' culture ministries backed its 2024 Wittgenstein exhibition.

name: Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky Zentrum
funding: Verein Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky Club is funded by Stadt Wien, Bezirk Margareten, the federal arts ministry, GESIBA and arching. ORF named Wertinvest, the building's owner, a financial backer in 2021.

name: Villa Beer
funding: Lothar Trierenberg, of an Upper Austrian paper family, bought the house for EUR 5M and spent twice that restoring it. Stadt Wien gave EUR 700k, the Monuments Office about 200k.

name: Braemhuis (Renaat Braem Huis)
funding: Herita vzw, a heritage non-profit, runs it with the City of Antwerp. The Flemish Government set EUR 6.3M for Herita's 2025 operating year under a one-year agreement.

name: Horta Museum
funding: The commune of Saint-Gilles bought the house in 1961. The museum's EUR 800k renewal is paid by Urban Brussels, the commune, Fonds Baillet-Latour, museum resources and an unnamed patron.

name: Van Buuren Museum & Gardens
funding: Lombard Odier is the structural partner. urban.brussels, Loterie Nationale and Uccle are institutional partners. Friends pay EUR 150 a year, patrons from EUR 2,000.
